title: Mushroom and Thyme Tart
subtitle: Rustic free-form tart with chestnut mushrooms and a creamy egg filling
excerpt: A rough-puff pastry base filled with sauteed chestnut mushrooms, thyme, and a simple cream and egg custard. No tart tin needed. Roll, fill, and fold the edges for a relaxed result that works for lunch or dinner.
sourceNotes: Free-form savoury tarts, sometimes called galettes, are a French bistro staple. The rough-puff method produces flaky layers without the precision of classical puff pastry.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry can be made and rested in the fridge for up to 2 hours before rolling.

content.text: Cook the mushrooms until all their liquid has evaporated and they are starting to colour. Wet mushrooms will make the pastry soggy.

items.prepNote: 1 for custard, 1 beaten for egg wash

content.text: Make the pastry. Rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture looks like rough breadcrumbs with some larger butter flakes still visible.
Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of ice-cold water. Mix until the dough just comes together. Do not overwork it.
Wrap and rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the mushrooms and thyme. Cook on a high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until all moisture has gone.
Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute. Season well. Leave to cool slightly.
Whisk the cream, 1 egg, and parmesan together. Season.
Roll the pastry out on a floured surface to a rough 35cm circle.
Slide onto a lined baking tray. Spread the mushrooms over the centre, leaving a 5cm border.
Pour the cream mixture over the mushrooms.
Fold the pastry edges up and over the filling. Brush the edges with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is just set.

items.symptom: Pastry base is soggy and undercooked.
items.cause: Mushrooms released moisture into the filling during baking.
items.fix: Cook mushrooms until completely dry before adding to the tart.

items.symptom: Pastry tears when folding up the edges.
items.cause: The dough was too thin or too cold and stiff.
items.fix: Let the dough rest at room temperature for 5 minutes before folding.
